root_cause.text: AppArmor’s apparmorfs released references to objects stored in inode->i_private at file-removal time instead of inode eviction, causing a use-after-free race because the VFS inode and later fs callbacks could outlive the dentry removal and still access i_private.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states “the inode can and does live beyond that point” and that callbacks may run “after the reference has been put,” and the patch fixes this by adding .evict_inode = aafs_evict to call aa_put_common_ref(inode->i_private) there while removing the earlier aa_put_* calls from remove_rawdata_dents(), __aafs_profile_rmdir(), and __aafs_ns_rmdir().

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit explicitly states “the inode can and does live beyond that point” and that callbacks may run “after the reference has been put,” and the patch fixes this by adding .evict_inode = aafs_evict to call aa_put_common_ref(inode->i_private) there while removing the earlier aa_put_* calls from remove_rawdata_dents(), __aafs_profile_rmdir(), and __aafs_ns_rmdir().

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the lib.h header so this file can use library declarations provided there during compilation.
intent_record.what: A single preprocessor include directive was added to include "include/lib.h" alongside the existing header includes in the source file.
intent_record.how: This makes declarations, macros, or inline helpers from include/lib.h available during compilation of this file, enabling use of those interfaces and preventing potential compile-time issues from missing declarations if they are referenced.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a named poison constant for invalid reference-state handling.
intent_record.what: A new preprocessor macro definition, `#define IREF_POISON 101`, was added near the top of the file before the support function section.
intent_record.how: This introduces a named constant that can be used elsewhere in the file or compilation unit as a poison marker value, enabling code to tag or detect invalid reference states instead of relying on an unnamed literal.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add typed common-ref helpers and an inode eviction cleanup path so AppArmor AAFS inodes correctly release referenced namespace, proxy, or loaddata objects.
intent_record.what: The change adds several new static helper functions: converters from struct aa_common_ref * to namespace, proxy, and loaddata objects using container_of and corresponding get functions; a reference-release helper aa_put_common_ref() that switches on ref->reftype and calls the matching put function; a reference-acquire helper aa_get_common_ref() that does kref_get(&ref->count); and a new aafs_evict(struct inode *inode) function that reads inode->i_private as an aa_common_ref, calls clear_inode(inode), drops the reference with aa_put_common_ref(ref), and poisons inode->i_private afterward.
intent_record.how: At runtime this introduces explicit generic reference management for objects stored in inode->i_private and provides an inode eviction path that releases the correct underlying AppArmor object when the inode is evicted. It prevents leaked references and ensures cleanup is matched to the referenced object's type, while also poisoning the private pointer after release to help catch misuse.

intent_record.intent_summary: Register the aafs inode eviction handler so AAFS performs proper filesystem-specific cleanup when inodes are evicted.
intent_record.what: A new superblock operation assignment was added to the aafs_super_ops structure: .evict_inode = aafs_evict, while the existing .statfs, .free_inode, and .show_path entries remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the filesystem will now invoke aafs_evict when an inode is evicted, enabling custom inode eviction and cleanup behavior during inode lifecycle teardown instead of relying on the absence of a filesystem-specific evict handler.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor aafs_create to use a typed aa_common_ref data parameter instead of a generic void pointer for stronger type safety.
intent_record.what: The function signature of aafs_create was changed so that the data parameter type is narrowed from a generic void * to a specific struct aa_common_ref *, with the parameter list also reformatted across lines; all other parameters remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime this makes the function accept only aa_common_ref-typed data instead of arbitrary pointers, improving type safety and ensuring callers pass the expected object type for internal use, while not otherwise altering the function's control flow in this diff hunk.

intent_record.intent_summary: Take a reference on non-NULL data in aafs_create() after successful creation to preserve object lifetime and avoid missing reference handling.
intent_record.what: A new conditional block was added before returning from aafs_create(): if the data pointer is non-NULL, aa_get_common_ref(data) is called.
intent_record.how: On successful creation, the function now increments or acquires the common reference associated with data before returning, preserving the lifetime of the referenced object and preventing it from being used without a held reference when data is supplied.

intent_record.intent_summary: Narrow aafs_create_file's data parameter from a generic void pointer to struct aa_common_ref for stronger type safety without changing behavior.
intent_record.what: The function signature of aafs_create_file was changed so that the data parameter is split onto its own line and its type is changed from void * to struct aa_common_ref *; the call to aafs_create still passes data unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, aafs_create_file now accepts only a struct aa_common_ref pointer for its data argument instead of an arbitrary pointer, tightening the interface with stronger type checking while preserving the same forwarding behavior to aafs_create.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the common namespace reference helper in profile_load() so policy loading acquires the correct namespace reference from inode private data.
intent_record.what: The local namespace reference acquisition in profile_load() was changed from calling aa_get_ns(f->f_inode->i_private) to calling get_ns_common_ref(f->f_inode->i_private), with no other code in the function modified.
intent_record.how: At runtime, profile_load() now obtains its namespace reference through a different helper, which changes how the inode private namespace pointer is interpreted or referenced and ensures the function uses the common namespace reference acquisition path before passing the namespace to policy_update().

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the common namespace reference helper in profile_replace() so policy replacement runs against the correctly referenced namespace.
intent_record.what: The namespace reference acquisition in profile_replace() was changed from aa_get_ns(f->f_inode->i_private) to get_ns_common_ref(f->f_inode->i_private), while leaving the rest of the function, including policy_update() and aa_put_ns(ns), unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, profile_replace() now obtains the namespace pointer through a different helper that likely acquires the appropriate common namespace reference for the inode's private data, ensuring the subsequent policy update operates on the correct referenced namespace object and matching the existing release path with aa_put_ns(ns).

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the common namespace reference helper in profile_remove() to obtain the correct namespace reference during profile removal.
intent_record.what: The initialization of the local namespace pointer in profile_remove() was changed from calling aa_get_ns(f->f_inode->i_private) to calling get_ns_common_ref(f->f_inode->i_private).
intent_record.how: At runtime, profile_remove() now acquires the namespace reference through a different helper, which likely standardizes or corrects how a common reference is obtained from inode private data before the rest of the profile removal logic runs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the common namespace reference helper when opening namespace revision data so inode private data is resolved correctly before falling back to the current namespace.
intent_record.what: The assignment of rev->ns in ns_revision_open() was changed from calling aa_get_ns(inode->i_private) to calling get_ns_common_ref(inode->i_private), while keeping the existing fallback to aa_get_current_ns() when the result is NULL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, ns_revision_open() now acquires the namespace reference from inode->i_private through get_ns_common_ref() instead of aa_get_ns(), which changes how the namespace object is resolved or referenced before the fallback path; this fixes namespace retrieval/reference handling for that inode data while preserving the fallback to the current namespace if no namespace is obtained.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the common proxy reference helper in `seq_profile_open()` so the seq file open path acquires the correct proxy reference from `inode->i_private`.
intent_record.what: The code changes the initialization of the local variable `proxy` in `seq_profile_open()` from calling `aa_get_proxy(inode->i_private)` to calling `get_proxy_common_ref(inode->i_private)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, `seq_profile_open()` now acquires the proxy reference through a different helper, which likely changes the reference acquisition semantics for `inode->i_private` so the object used by `single_open()` is obtained in a safer or more appropriate way.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the common loaddata reference helper in seq_rawdata_open() so the seq file open path acquires the correct loaddata object safely.
intent_record.what: In seq_rawdata_open(), the initialization of the local variable `data` was changed from calling `aa_get_i_loaddata(inode->i_private)` to calling `get_loaddata_common_ref(inode->i_private)` with the same argument.
intent_record.how: At runtime, seq_rawdata_open() now acquires the loaddata object through a different reference-acquisition helper, which changes how the object is looked up or refcounted before the existing null check; this is intended to ensure the correct common reference is obtained when opening the seq file.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the correct helper to acquire a loaddata reference in rawdata_open() so the file open path gets the proper backing object.
intent_record.what: The call that retrieves the loaddata object in rawdata_open() was changed from aa_get_i_loaddata(inode->i_private) to get_loaddata_common_ref(inode->i_private), while the surrounding access check and NULL handling remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, rawdata_open() now obtains the loaddata reference through a different helper that likely returns a common/refcounted loaddata reference from inode->i_private, preserving the existing ENOENT path when no object is found but correcting how the object is acquired for subsequent use.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop dropping a loaddata reference for each removed rawdata dent to avoid incorrect reference counting during cleanup.
intent_record.what: The call to aa_put_i_loaddata(rawdata) was removed from inside the conditional block in remove_rawdata_dents(), leaving the code to only call aafs_remove(rawdata->dents[i]) and then set rawdata->dents[i] to NULL when the dent entry is valid.
intent_record.how: At runtime, removing directory entries no longer decrements the loaddata reference count for each removed dent, preventing premature reference release or over-decrementing during cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use rawdata's embedded reference count as the file private data and remove manual aa_get_i_loaddata() bumps to fix loaddata lifetime management for AppArmor rawdata fs entries.
intent_record.what: The function __aa_fs_create_rawdata() was changed to stop passing the rawdata pointer as the private data argument to aafs_create_file() for the "abi", "revision", optional "sha256", "compressed_size", and "raw_data" files, and instead pass &rawdata->count. In the same locations, the repeated aa_get_i_loaddata(rawdata) calls that followed each successful file creation were removed, while the directory and dent assignments remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the created AppArmor fs files now hold a reference to rawdata through its count field rather than requiring explicit per-file aa_get_i_loaddata() reference increments after creation. This changes ownership/lifetime handling so file creation relies on the embedded count-based object tracking, avoiding the previous manual reference bumps and preventing mismatched or redundant loaddata reference management.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the rawdata creation failure path by removing an erroneous loaddata release that could cause a double put or premature free.
intent_record.what: The failure path in __aa_fs_create_rawdata() was changed by deleting the call to aa_put_i_loaddata(rawdata) after remove_rawdata_dents(rawdata) and before returning PTR_ERR(dent).
intent_record.how: On error, the function no longer decrements or releases the rawdata loaddata object in this cleanup block, preventing that object from being freed or reference-dropped at this point and avoiding an incorrect extra release during failure handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop explicitly dropping the dentry's aa_proxy reference during profile dentry removal to avoid incorrect proxy lifetime handling.
intent_record.what: The loop that removes profile dentries no longer declares a local struct aa_proxy pointer, no longer reads d_inode(profile->dents[i])->i_private into that pointer, and no longer calls aa_put_proxy(proxy) after aafs_remove(profile->dents[i]); only the dentry removal and nulling of profile->dents[i] remain.
intent_record.how: At runtime, removing a profile directory entry no longer performs an explicit proxy reference decrement based on the dentry inode's private data. This avoids releasing the associated aa_proxy during this cleanup path, preventing an extra or misplaced put if ownership is already handled elsewhere.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor create_profile_file() to call aafs_create_file() directly with the profile proxy count instead of manually managing a proxy reference.
intent_record.what: The function create_profile_file() was simplified by removing the local aa_proxy *proxy variable, the temporary dentry *dent variable, the call to aa_get_proxy(profile->label.proxy), the conditional aa_put_proxy(proxy) on error, and the explicit return of dent; it now directly returns aafs_create_file(name, S_IFREG | 0444, dir, &profile->label.proxy->count, fops).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the file creation path no longer acquires and conditionally releases a proxy reference around aafs_create_file(); instead it passes the address of the proxy's count member directly to aafs_create_file, shifting lifetime/reference handling away from this helper and avoiding the previous get/put sequence in this function.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix rawdata_get_link_base() to recover aa_proxy from inode->i_private via its embedded aa_common_ref instead of incorrectly casting it directly.
intent_record.what: The local variable initialized from inode->i_private was changed from a direct struct aa_proxy * cast to first reading inode->i_private as a struct aa_common_ref * and then deriving the struct aa_proxy * with container_of(ref, struct aa_proxy, count).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now interprets inode->i_private as pointing to the embedded count field within aa_proxy rather than to the start of an aa_proxy object, allowing it to recover the containing aa_proxy correctly and avoiding use of an invalid direct pointer layout assumption.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix AppArmor raw-data symlink creation to track the proxy via its count field instead of taking extra proxy references.
intent_record.what: The calls to aafs_create() for the "raw_sha256", "raw_abi", and "raw_data" symlinks were changed to pass &profile->label.proxy->count as the fourth argument instead of profile->label.proxy, and the corresponding aa_get_proxy(profile->label.proxy) calls after each successful creation were removed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, these aafs entries now store a pointer to the proxy's reference count rather than the proxy object itself, and they no longer explicitly increment the proxy reference after creating each symlink. This changes lifetime management for the backing object, avoiding extra proxy reference acquisitions tied to these filesystem entries.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the common namespace reference helper in ns_mkdir_op() when obtaining the parent namespace.
intent_record.what: The code replaces the call to aa_get_ns(dir->i_private) with get_ns_common_ref(dir->i_private) when assigning the parent namespace reference in ns_mkdir_op().
intent_record.how: At runtime, ns_mkdir_op() now acquires the parent reference through a common namespace reference helper instead of the AppArmor-specific getter, which changes how the namespace object is referenced or validated before the subsequent consistency check and locking operations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the common namespace reference helper in `ns_rmdir_op()` so parent namespace references are acquired correctly during rmdir handling.
intent_record.what: The code changes the assignment of `parent` in `ns_rmdir_op()` from calling `aa_get_ns(dir->i_private)` to calling `get_ns_common_ref(dir->i_private)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, `parent` now obtains its namespace reference through a different reference-acquisition helper, which likely uses a common or updated reference-handling path for `dir->i_private` and changes how the namespace object's lifetime is protected during directory removal.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant namespace reference releases from __aafs_ns_rmdir() to avoid dropping aa_ns references twice during AppArmor filesystem namespace teardown.
intent_record.what: The change deletes five conditional blocks in __aafs_ns_rmdir() that checked ns_subns_dir(ns), ns_subload(ns), ns_subreplace(ns), ns_subremove(ns), and ns_subrevision(ns), retrieved each dentry inode's i_private into sub, and called aa_put_ns(sub) before the loop that removes ns->dents entries.
intent_record.how: At runtime, __aafs_ns_rmdir() no longer decrements namespace references stored in the i_private field of those specific dentries during namespace directory removal, leaving only the generic dent removal loop to run. This prevents those aa_put_ns() calls from occurring at this point, avoiding premature or duplicate namespace reference drops during teardown.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the unconfined label count as AppArmor filesystem entry private data instead of the namespace object and drop the now-unneeded namespace reference bumps.
intent_record.what: The code changes the private data passed to several AppArmor filesystem entries in __aafs_ns_mkdir_entries() from ns to &ns->unconfined->label.count for the files "revision", ".load", ".replace", ".remove", and the "namespaces" directory, and removes the corresponding aa_get_ns(ns) reference count increments after each successful creation.
intent_record.how: At runtime, these dentries/files now carry a pointer to the namespace's unconfined label count instead of the namespace object itself, so their lifetime tracking is tied to that label/count object rather than requiring explicit namespace reference acquisition here; removing aa_get_ns(ns) avoids taking extra namespace references that are no longer needed for these entries.

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch `aa_proxy` to use AppArmor's common reference-count structure instead of `kref` for unified internal refcount management.

intent_record.how: At runtime, `aa_proxy` now uses the AppArmor-specific common reference-counting structure instead of the generic kernel reference-counting type, enabling this object to participate in the subsystem's shared refcount handling semantics and any associated helper logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch aa_label reference counting from kref to aa_common_ref to align it with the subsystem's common reference infrastructure.
intent_record.what: The type of the aa_label struct member named count was changed from struct kref to struct aa_common_ref, with no other modifications shown in this hunk.
intent_record.how: At runtime, aa_label instances will use the aa_common_ref reference-counting mechanism instead of the generic kref type, enabling aa_label reference management to follow the subsystem's common reference abstraction and associated behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix __aa_get_label() to use the correct nested reference count field when safely acquiring a label reference.
intent_record.what: The call to kref_get_unless_zero() in __aa_get_label() was changed to pass &l->count.count instead of &l->count, leaving the surrounding null check and return logic unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now increments the reference count using the nested count field rather than the outer count member, ensuring the helper operates on the expected kref object layout and correctly acquires a label reference only when its count is nonzero.

intent_record.what: In aa_get_label(), the argument passed to kref_get() was changed from &(l->count) to &(l->count.count) inside the existing null check.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes aa_get_label() increment the nested kref field rather than the outer count member, ensuring the reference count update targets the correct object layout and preventing incorrect refcount handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix aa_label RCU reference acquisition by passing the nested kref count field to kref_get_unless_zero.
intent_record.what: The call inside the retry loop was changed from kref_get_unless_zero(&c->count) to kref_get_unless_zero(&c->count.count), replacing the address of the count field on aa_label with the address of its nested count member.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the reference acquisition now passes the expected underlying refcount object to kref_get_unless_zero, allowing the label's reference count to be incremented correctly under RCU instead of using the wrong structure field and risking failed or invalid refcount handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix aa_put_label to pass the embedded kref field to kref_put so label reference counting works correctly.
intent_record.what: The argument passed to kref_put in aa_put_label was changed from &l->count to &l->count.count, while keeping the surrounding null check and callback unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes kref_put operate on the actual embedded struct kref field instead of its containing count wrapper, ensuring reference count decrementation targets the correct object and preventing incorrect refcount handling or type misuse.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix aa_get_proxy() to increment the embedded kref in proxy->count correctly.
intent_record.what: The inline function aa_get_proxy() was changed so that the kref_get() call now passes &(proxy->count.count) instead of &(proxy->count).
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes kref_get() operate on the actual embedded struct kref field rather than the surrounding count member object, ensuring the proxy reference count is incremented using the correct type and memory location.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix aa_put_proxy() to pass the embedded kref to kref_put so proxy reference counting works correctly.
intent_record.what: The call to kref_put in aa_put_proxy() was changed from passing &proxy->count to passing &proxy->count.count, while keeping the surrounding null check and callback unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, aa_put_proxy() now decrements the actual embedded kref object expected by kref_put instead of passing the containing field, ensuring correct reference count handling and proper release callback invocation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a shared typed reference-counting structure for AppArmor aafs data objects.
intent_record.what: The change adds a new enum named reftype with three values (REF_NS, REF_PROXY, REF_RAWDATA) and introduces a new struct aa_common_ref containing a struct kref field named count and an enum reftype field named reftype, along with a comment indicating it is a common reference count for data shown up in aafs.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this enables AppArmor code to associate a standardized reference-counting object with multiple data types and track what kind of referenced object is being managed, supporting shared lifetime management infrastructure for aafs-exposed data.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix aa_get_profile() to increment the correct embedded kref for AppArmor profile reference counting.
intent_record.what: The call inside aa_get_profile() was changed from kref_get(&(p->label.count)) to kref_get(&(p->label.count.count)) when p is non-NULL.
intent_record.how: This makes the function increment the actual embedded kref object rather than its containing count field, ensuring the profile reference count is updated on the correct structure at runtime.

intent_record.what: The code changes the argument passed to kref_get_unless_zero() in aa_get_profile_not0() from &p->label.count to &p->label.count.count.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes kref_get_unless_zero() operate on the actual embedded kref field instead of its containing wrapper/member, ensuring the reference count is accessed correctly and preventing incorrect refcount handling when trying to acquire a profile reference only if it is nonzero.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix aa_get_profile_rcu() to acquire a reference from the actual nested kref field so profile refcounting works correctly under RCU.
intent_record.what: The code changes the argument passed to kref_get_unless_zero() in aa_get_profile_rcu() from &c->label.count to &c->label.count.count, replacing a pointer to the label's count field with a pointer to its nested count member.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes kref_get_unless_zero() operate on the actual embedded kref object rather than the surrounding wrapper field, allowing the reference count to be incremented correctly when the profile is still alive and preventing incorrect refcount handling or type misuse.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix `aa_put_profile` to decrement the profile label's actual `kref` field instead of the enclosing count member.
intent_record.what: The `aa_put_profile` helper was changed so that `kref_put` now receives `&p->label.count.count` instead of `&p->label.count` when `p` is non-NULL.
intent_record.how: At runtime this makes `kref_put` operate on the actual embedded `struct kref` field rather than its containing wrapper/member, ensuring the profile's reference count is decremented through the correct object and avoiding incorrect refcount handling or type/layout mismatches.

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch `aa_loaddata.count` from `kref` to `aa_common_ref` to use AppArmor's common reference-counting infrastructure.
intent_record.what: The type of the `count` field in `struct aa_loaddata` was changed from `struct kref` to `struct aa_common_ref`, while the surrounding fields and structure layout remain otherwise unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, references tracked through `count` will now use the `aa_common_ref` reference-management mechanism instead of the generic `kref` type, enabling this field to participate in AppArmor-specific common reference handling semantics rather than plain kernel reference counting.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix aa_get_i_loaddata() to increment the correct embedded kref when taking a reference to loaddata.
intent_record.what: The call to kref_get in aa_get_i_loaddata() was changed from passing &data->count to passing &data->count.count.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the reference increment is now applied to the actual embedded kref field expected by kref_get instead of the outer count member, preventing an incorrect type/field access and ensuring the loaddata object's reference count is incremented correctly when data is non-NULL.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix aa_put_i_loaddata to pass the embedded kref to kref_put so loaddata reference counting works correctly.
intent_record.what: The call to kref_put in aa_put_i_loaddata was changed from passing &data->count to passing &data->count.count, while keeping the surrounding null check and callback unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes kref_put operate on the actual embedded struct kref object instead of its containing count field wrapper, ensuring the reference count is decremented on the correct object and the release callback is triggered correctly when the count reaches zero.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix aa_proxy_kref() to recover the aa_proxy object from the nested kref field using count.count so reference release operates on the correct structure.
intent_record.what: The container_of() call in aa_proxy_kref() was changed to use the nested member path count.count instead of count when deriving struct aa_proxy *proxy from the kref pointer, with the line split across two lines for formatting.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes container_of() compute the enclosing aa_proxy address from the actual embedded struct kref field inside the nested count member, so the callback receives the correct parent object address and avoids freeing or accessing the wrong memory.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix proxy allocation to correctly initialize the embedded reference counter and mark it as a proxy reference type.
intent_record.what: The initialization of the proxy reference counter was changed from calling kref_init on new->count to calling it on the nested field new->count.count, and a new assignment was added to set new->count.reftype = REF_PROXY before storing the label pointer.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this initializes the actual embedded kref inside the count structure and tags the reference object as a proxy, ensuring the proxy's reference counting metadata is set up correctly for later retain/release handling instead of leaving the nested refcount type information uninitialized or initializing the wrong object.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix aa_label_kref() to recover the correct aa_label from a nested kref member by using count.count in container_of.

intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes the offset used by container_of so the aa_label pointer is computed from the actual embedded kref field inside a nested count member, preventing recovery of an incorrect parent pointer and ensuring subsequent namespace lookup and label release logic operate on the correct aa_label object.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix label reference-count initialization by targeting the embedded kref and setting the reference type metadata for aafs use.
intent_record.what: The initialization of the label reference count was changed from calling kref_init on label->count to calling it on the nested field label->count.count, and a new assignment was added to set label->count.reftype = REF_NS.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this initializes the embedded kref inside a structured reference-count container rather than treating the whole container as a kref, and it also records the reference type as REF_NS so the label carries the expected refcount metadata for aafs-related handling.

intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes container_of() compute the enclosing struct aa_loaddata address from the actual embedded kref field inside the nested count member, so the callback receives the correct parent object pointer and avoids freeing or accessing the wrong memory.

intent_record.intent_summary: Correct loaddata reference initialization by initializing the embedded kref field and assigning the raw-data reference type.
intent_record.what: The initialization of the loaddata reference counter was changed from calling kref_init on d->count to calling kref_init on the nested field d->count.count, and a new assignment was added to set d->count.reftype = REF_RAWDATA.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this initializes the actual embedded kref inside a composite reference-tracking structure and tags that reference with the REF_RAWDATA type, ensuring the reference state is set up consistently and correctly for later reference-count operations and type-aware handling.

grouping_result.intent: Add the lib.h header so this file can use library declarations provided there during compilation.
Add a named poison constant for invalid reference-state handling.
